claims.text: The controlled intervention is rapid thermal annealing at 250–350 °C for 30–60 seconds under inert atmosphere with an approximately 50 °C/s ramp rate.
The as-deposited FeMnNiGeSi films or nanoribbons have high residual stress.
The as-deposited material has confined grain structures.
The as-deposited material has inherent chemical inhomogeneities.
The specified rapid thermal annealing treatment relieves residual stress in the FeMnNiGeSi films or nanoribbons.
Rapid thermal annealing partially relaxes grain boundaries.
Rapid thermal annealing refines or adjusts short-range chemical ordering.
Relieving internal stress and modifying nanoscale heterogeneities reduces magnetic domain-wall pinning.
Reduced domain-wall pinning lowers energy barriers for magnetic reorientation.
Higher residual stress in the as-deposited samples causes stronger domain-wall pinning.
Stronger domain-wall pinning in the as-deposited samples produces broader magnetic hysteresis loops.
Annealed samples will exhibit narrower hysteresis loops and reduced coercivity relative to the as-deposited baseline.
Annealing will shift the temperature of the peak magnetocaloric entropy change.
Annealing will improve cycle-to-cycle reproducibility of the magnetocaloric response.
Temperature-dependent M(H) data can be used to calculate magnetocaloric entropy change using Maxwell relations.
Heat-transfer rates limit the permissible magnetic-cooling cycle frequency in the proposed operating regime.
Excessive annealing can cause unwanted grain growth or phase changes that must be avoided.

contradictions.description: The boundary excludes annealing conditions that cause grain growth or phase changes, but the falsification rule treats observing those out-of-boundary effects as falsification rather than as failure to implement the intervention within its stated applicability.
